newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends stronger on certification hopes.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends stronger on certification hopes.

text.p: The Mexican peso clawed back some lost ground at the close on Friday.
Traders said the peso recovered as banks that had gone long on dollars stepped in to sell them ahead of expected recertification by the U.S. government of Mexico as an ally in the the war on drugs.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended 3.4 and 2.5 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.9400/7.9460 and 7.9350/7.9450 per dollar.
"The peso recovered as the market has already discounted Mexico's certification," a trader said.
News that U.S. Secretary of State Albright recommended recertification for Mexico came just five minutes after the close of trade in Mexico's foreign exchange markets.
Traders noted Banco de Mexico did not intervene in the market as speculation had eased considerably since Thursday.

The central bank was expected to accept bids from banks to buy dollars if the peso reached a rate of 7.9925 per dollar by 1200 local time/1800 GMT, or two percent weaker than the official fixing rate published in Friday's edition of the Mexican Government Official Gazette.
This rate was surpassed in early trade, but the peso began to firm up mid-morning so the criteria for central bank intervention never crystallized.
Traders said they expected more banks to sell more long dollar positions on Monday after certification was confirmed.

"Yesterday's (peso) onslaught was out of order. Dealers overbought dollars and they dumped part of their positions today," another dealer said. "So now we have certification, they will certainly offload the rest on Monday."
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 14 centavos weaker at 7.9550/7.9650 per dollar, after lagging the market.
